title: Review: the uncovered test_measure group, synthetic_reference profile (13 records; 8 source-grounded citations re-derived against the pinned blob)

revision_history.author: reviewer_automated
revision_history.description: Initial revision. Reviews the 13 uncovered test_measure records in the synthetic_reference profile. Records four findings, two of them medium. Records one candidate finding that a second read showed was not a defect and WITHDREW it rather than softening it. Changes no test_measure record and revises no engineering content. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false.

lifecycle_status_note: Set to the value above because this review did read the records it names and the digests below were computed from the bytes on disk at authoring time. It is NOT a statement about engineering validity, organisational independence or human confirmation, and this review is not a signature. No human read any record covered here.
scope: TARGETED SCOPE: the test_measure records in the synthetic_reference profile that no review record covered, and nothing else. That is 13 records: FB2-VER-TMS-000001 through -000005 and -000021 through -000028. PROFILE-SCOPED, and the reason is measured rather than assumed: the coverage dimension is computed on UNIQUE ID STRINGS, so five of these thirteen identifiers (FB2-VER-TMS-000001 to -000005) already read as covered because an as_is record carries the same id. They are still reviewed here, because under ID-RULE-004-A1 the pair (profile, id) is the key and a digest is a statement about one record, not about an identifier. NOT COVERED HERE AND NOT CLAIMED: the 12 uncovered requirement records, the 12 uncovered singleton-family records, the 35 uncovered finding records, the 18 uncovered scenario records, the 20 uncovered review records and the 12 uncovered execution records. Those are named in limitations.

reviewer_identity.note: Automated review performed in a single AI coding-agent session (opencode). The model identifier is the identifier exposed to this session's runtime. No platform-issued session id was available to the reviewer, so session_id is a locally chosen label for this run and is not a platform-issued identifier. This is an AUTOMATED REVIEW: it is NOT organizational independence, NOT human confirmation and NOT a qualified-checker result. No human reviewer, no independent party and no separate agent session participated. Consistent with corpus-policy.json#/review_policy/ai_review_limitations, a distinct agent session would not have been independence either.

review_method: The 13 records were READ in full, field by field, and the machine-checkable claims were re-derived rather than accepted. (1) The two populations inside the family were separated before anything was reported, because they are not the same kind of record: five records dated 2026-09-13 carry a boilerplate revision_history entry, no oracle_detail, no lifecycle_status_note and an empty limitations array, while eight records dated 2026-10-02 each carry a four-field oracle_detail, a four-item limitations array and a lifecycle_status_note. Judging the family as one kind of record would have produced findings that were false of eight of the thirteen. (2) Every expected_outcomes entry in all 13 records was set beside the steps array of the same record, outcome by outcome, to establish what the record's machine-readable oracle actually encodes. (3) Every source-grounded claim in the eight newer records was re-derived against the PINNED source with 'git show 308028fb:<path>': the cited line range was read, the cited symbol was located in the file, and the mechanism the record attributes to that range was compared with what the range contains. Seven distinct citations were checked and six verify exactly; the seventh is FB2-REV-FND-000175. (4) The one analytical-model claim that rests on a corpus value rather than on code, FB2-VER-TMS-000022's 50 ms acquisition period, was re-read out of the parameter registry rather than taken from the record. (5) The claim that no record in this family is covered by any review was not taken from the coverage figure: it was measured directly against the review records and the reviewed_by link registry, and the lifecycle_status of every uncovered record in the whole corpus was tallied, which is how FB2-REV-FND-000174 got its corpus-wide figure.

findings.description: Five records in this family assert a review state that no review record supports, and no automated control can detect it. FB2-VER-TMS-000001, -000002, -000003, -000004 and -000005 each carry lifecycle_status 'reviewed'. Before this review existed, NONE of the five was named by any review record or by any reviewed_by link: they were all in the uncovered population this review was scoped to. So 'reviewed' was a claim about a review that did not exist. Three further facts make it worse rather than better, and all three are measured, not inferred. (1) Each of the five carries automated_review_status with schema_valid, links_valid, provenance_consistent and consistency_checks all true and last_run 2026-09-13T00:00:00Z - the same instant as its own created_at, so the flags were authored rather than produced by a later run. (2) None of the five carries a lifecycle_status_note. The eight sibling records in the SAME family, dated 2026-10-02, each carry a lifecycle_status_note that says in terms that no human has reviewed the record and that automated_review_status refers to corpus automation and is not a statement about engineering validity or human confirmation. The correction is therefore already written, in this very family, and these five do not have it. (3) None of the five carries a limitations array at all, while each of the eight carries four limitations. THE CONTROL GAP, which is the part that outlives these five records: I searched the suite for any rule relating lifecycle_status 'reviewed' to the existence of a covering review record and found none. A record can therefore be marked reviewed, forever, with nothing behind it and the suite stays green. I measured the size of that gap across the whole corpus: 22 of 323 records assert lifecycle_status 'reviewed' with no covering review record, of which only 3 carry any lifecycle_status_note, so 19 are silent about it. By family: execution 12, test_measure 5, review 3, unit_test_specification 1, finding 1. By profile: as_is 14, synthetic_reference 8. NOT CLAIMED: no record's engineering content is wrong, no oracle is wrong, no digest is wrong, and no safety-relevant statement depends on any of it. The defect is that a review-state field reads as a fact about the corpus when it is an unverified assertion, on a field the other eight records in the same family show is capable of carrying the honest value 'draft' with a note explaining it.
findings.evidence: Directly measured, not inferred. For each of the 13 records: lifecycle_status, presence of lifecycle_status_note, len(limitations), and automated_review_status. FB2-VER-TMS-000001 through -000005: lifecycle_status 'reviewed', note ABSENT, limitations length 0, automated_review_status all four flags true with last_run 2026-09-13T00:00:00Z equal to their created_at. FB2-VER-TMS-000021 through -000028: lifecycle_status 'draft', note PRESENT, limitations length 4 each, last_run 2026-10-02T00:00:00Z. Coverage: the union of every reviewed_ids entry across the 20 review records that existed before this one and of every reviewed_by target_id in docs/artifacts/traceability/link-registry/ names none of the five; after this review the five are named by it. Corpus-wide tally: iterate load_artifact_index(), keep records whose lifecycle_status == 'reviewed', subtract the covered set, count 22, of which 3 carry a lifecycle_status_note. Control search: 'lifecycle_status' appears in docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py in no expression that compares it to a review record's existence, and the gate at the automated_review_coverage dimension reads only review records and reviewed_by links, never the per-record lifecycle_status field. This review changed nothing.

findings.description: One source-grounded oracle attributes to the wrong function a flag that function does not set. The record's oracle_detail.why_this_oracle reads: "'A transferred value whose recomputed packet error code differs from the received one is marked invalid, and an invalid value is not consumed by a decision' is what LTC_CheckPec (ltc_6813-1.c:3838-3878) and the invalidCellVoltage flag it sets at line 641 do." Three checks against the pinned blob. (1) LTC_CheckPec at ltc_6813-1.c:3838-3878 is cited exactly right - line 3838 is the definition, line 3878 its closing brace, and the body is the per-LTC loop the record describes. (2) That body contains ZERO occurrences of the identifier invalidCellVoltage. It writes errorTable->PEC_valid[stringNumber][i] and nothing else; the word 'it' in 'the invalidCellVoltage flag it sets' therefore names a function that does not set that flag. (3) Line 641 is a real line inside the real file, so the citation is not a dangling reference - it is simply in a different function. Line 641 sits inside LTC_SaveVoltages, which begins at line 597, roughly 3200 lines below LTC_CheckPec, and its surrounding branch is the OPEN-WIRE else-path, whose own comment at line 640 reads 'Set cell voltage measurement value invalid, if not already invalid because of PEC Error'. The two sites are peers, not one: LTC_SaveVoltages handles open-wire and range plausibility, and sets invalidCellVoltage at line 636 on a plausibility failure and at line 641 on an open-wire condition. THE SUBSTANTIVE CLAIM SURVIVES, and this review says so explicitly because it is the part that matters: the propagation the record asserts is real and I found it. The actual site is ltc_6813-1.c:3114-3130, in the voltage-extraction loop, where the code tests errorTable->PEC_valid[stringNumber][m] and, when it is false, both SKIPS storing cellVoltage_mV and sets invalidCellVoltage to true for that register's cells. The record's expected outcome corrupted_frames_consumed_unchallenged = '0' is therefore reachable, and its 'decided before use' claim is sound at the pinned commit. LTC_DISCARD_PEC is (false) in src/app/driver/afe/ltc/6813-1/config/ltc_6813-1_cfg.h:106, so the branch that marks the frame invalid is the one the build takes. So this is a CITATION-ATTRIBUTION defect in a reviewable record whose substantive claim holds, not a provenance failure and not an over-claiming oracle. Severity is low for that reason, and it would be dishonest to raise it higher. The record's own residual_risk already discloses the general shape of the exposure - that a source-grounded oracle rests on the code doing what the authoring pass read it to do - but it does not name the conditionality on LTC_DISCARD_PEC, and it attributes the flag to the wrong function.
findings.evidence: Read with 'git show 308028fb13d046ba29b98886895c2e17937b1437:src/app/driver/afe/ltc/6813-1/ltc_6813-1.c', 4860 lines. Lines 3838-3878 are LTC_CheckPec: signature at 3838, 'for (uint16_t i = 0u; i < LTC_N_LTC; i++)' at 3850, the PEC comparison at 3863-3864, the LTC_DISCARD_PEC branch at 3866-3871, return at 3877, closing brace at 3878. A grep for invalidCellVoltage over exactly those 41 lines returns 0 matches. The file's own use of invalidCellVoltage outside that range is at lines 623, 636, 641, 3118-3122 and 3126-3129. The nearest function signature at or before line 641 is 'extern void LTC_SaveVoltages(LTC_STATE_s *ltc_state, uint8_t stringNumber)' at line 597, so line 641 is inside LTC_SaveVoltages and inside the else-branch whose comment at line 640 names the open-wire case. The real PEC-to-invalid site is lines 3114-3131: 'if (ltc_state->ltcData.errorTable->PEC_valid[stringNumber][m] == true)' at 3114 stores cellVoltage_mV and clears invalidCellVoltage at 3118-3122, and the else at 3124-3130 sets invalidCellVoltage true without storing the value. LTC_DISCARD_PEC is defined '(false)' at src/app/driver/afe/ltc/6813-1/config/ltc_6813-1_cfg.h:106 at the same pin. This review changed nothing.

findings.description: In five of the thirteen records the machine-readable oracle encodes only the expected path, so the case that gives the test its distinguishing power has no expected value. The defect is systematic and it is in the same five records FB2-REV-FND-000174 names. Set each record's steps beside its own expected_outcomes. FB2-VER-TMS-000001 has three steps; step 3 injects a voltage within limits and expects 'No fault triggered', and the array holds exactly two outcomes, fault_request = 'true' and violation_type = 'OVERVOLTAGE'. Neither can express step 3, and both describe step 2. FB2-VER-TMS-000003 has two steps; step 2 injects an out-of-range 4900 mV and expects 'Flagged implausible', and the array holds exactly one outcome, plausibility_result = 'pass', which is step 1's expectation. A test whose entire purpose is that 4900 mV is REJECTED has as its only recorded oracle that 3300 mV is ACCEPTED, so it would pass against an implementation that accepted everything. FB2-VER-TMS-000002 is the same shape and worse: step 1 expects 'Transitions match state table' and no outcome corresponds to it, and the state table the step defers to is not in the record, so the record's primary oracle points at an artefact that does not exist in it. THIS IS NOT A SCHEMA LIMITATION AND NOT MY JUDGEMENT OF WHAT A TEST SHOULD CONTAIN, and the family itself proves both: the eight newer records use the same expected_outcomes structure to encode exactly the negative case the older five omit. FB2-VER-TMS-000028 records limit_entries_raised_while_invalid = '0' with unit 'entries', which is the invalid-data case; FB2-VER-TMS-000024 records soa_debounce_state_found_in_source = '0' with unit 'occurrences', which is the absence case; FB2-VER-TMS-000021 records corrupted_frames_consumed_unchallenged = '0' with unit 'frames'. Corroborating evidence that the five older records are template instances rather than measures written about their own subject: tolerances is the identical object {"value": "exact"} in all five, and timing is byte-identical in all five (max_execution_time_ms 100, setup_time_ms 10, teardown_time_ms 5) - so the record-level timing budget of 100 ms is both uninformative for each measure and looser than the only timing assertion two of the five actually make (FB2-VER-TMS-000002's contactor_open_latency_ms < 50 and FB2-VER-TMS-000004's independent_open_latency_ms < 80). FB2-VER-TMS-000001 states an objective of 'Verify SOA voltage limit detection accuracy and latency' and contains no accuracy tolerance anywhere. NOT CLAIMED: nothing here says the tests would fail, nothing says the recorded outcomes are false, and nothing says the tests are worthless - steps and expected prose are present and readable. The defect is that a reader or a harness that trusts expected_outcomes reads a weaker claim than the record's own steps state.
findings.evidence: Parsed steps[] and expected_outcomes[] of all 13 records and compared them pairwise. FB2-VER-TMS-000001: 3 steps, 2 outcomes, step 3 ('No fault triggered') unrepresented. FB2-VER-TMS-000002: 3 steps, 2 outcomes, step 1 ('Transitions match state table') unrepresented; the string 'state table' occurs nowhere else in the record and no field carries such a table. FB2-VER-TMS-000003: 2 steps, 1 outcome, step 2 ('Flagged implausible') unrepresented. FB2-VER-TMS-000004: 3 steps, 2 outcomes, step 1 ('Monitor path triggers independent open') has no distinct outcome though path_independent partially covers it. FB2-VER-TMS-000005: 3 steps, 2 outcomes, step 2 ('Error counter increments') unrepresented. By contrast FB2-VER-TMS-000021 has 4 steps and 4 outcomes including corrupted_frames_consumed_unchallenged = '0'; FB2-VER-TMS-000024 has 4 steps and 4 outcomes including soa_debounce_state_found_in_source = '0'; FB2-VER-TMS-000028 has 5 steps and 4 outcomes including limit_entries_raised_while_invalid = '0'. Tolerances and timing objects compared by value across the five older records: tolerances is {"value": "exact"} in all five; timing is {max_execution_time_ms: 100, setup_time_ms: 10, teardown_time_ms: 5} in all five; the eight newer records each carry a distinct tolerances object and a distinct timing object. This review changed nothing.

findings.description: Two records label an inequality as though it were an equality, in the one field that is supposed to say how the comparison is to be judged. FB2-VER-TMS-000002 records expected_outcomes[0] as {signal: contactor_open_latency_ms, expected_value: '<50', tolerance: 'exact', unit: 'ms'}. FB2-VER-TMS-000004 records {signal: independent_open_latency_ms, expected_value: '<80', tolerance: 'exact', unit: 'ms'}. The expected_value is an ordering relation, so 'exact' describes no possible outcome: a measured 49 ms and a measured 12 ms are equally not 'exact'. Read together with the record-level tolerances object, which in both records is the same uninformative {"value": "exact"} that FB2-REV-FND-000176 names, the record ends up asserting exactness in three places while its only timing claim is an inequality. THE FIELD IS USED CORRECTLY ELSEWHERE IN THE SAME FAMILY, which is what makes this an authoring inconsistency rather than a vocabulary limitation: FB2-VER-TMS-000022 pairs expected_value '20' with tolerance 'at least'; FB2-VER-TMS-000025 pairs tolerance 'outside' and 'at least' with expected values that are relations in words; FB2-VER-TMS-000028 pairs expected_value 'at least 1' with tolerance 'at least'. So the corpus already has a working convention for a bounded assertion and these two records do not use it. CONSEQUENCE, stated at its real size: a harness that evaluates tolerance == 'exact' as string equality would reject every possible measurement of these two outcomes, and a harness that ignores the tolerance would compare the string '<50' to a number. Either way the timing assertions of these two measures are not machine-evaluable as written. NOT CLAIMED: no threshold is wrong - '<50' and '<80' are also the figures their own steps state in prose, the values are consistent with each other, and no engineering content is affected.
findings.evidence: expected_outcomes of FB2-VER-TMS-000002: [{signal: contactor_open_latency_ms, expected_value: '<50', tolerance: 'exact', unit: 'ms'}, {signal: fault_feedback_diag, expected_value: 'true', tolerance: 'exact', unit: 'bool'}]; step 2 of the same record states 'Open contactors within 50 ms', so the prose and the outcome agree on the number. expected_outcomes of FB2-VER-TMS-000004: [{signal: independent_open_latency_ms, expected_value: '<80', tolerance: 'exact', unit: 'ms'}, {signal: path_independent, expected_value: 'true', tolerance: 'exact', unit: 'bool'}]; step 2 states 'Contactors opened within 80 ms'. Contrast within the same family: FB2-VER-TMS-000022 expected_values '20'/'0'/'50' with tolerances 'at least'/'at least'/'at most'; FB2-VER-TMS-000025 tolerances 'at least'/'outside'/'exact'; FB2-VER-TMS-000028 expected_value 'at least 1' with tolerance 'at least'. Affected records are 2 of 13; the other 11 use a tolerance consistent with their expected_value. This review changed nothing.

dispositions.action: Accepted, in two separable parts. (1) For the five records named, set lifecycle_status to the value the record can support and add the lifecycle_status_note the eight siblings already carry; the honest value is 'draft' unless a review record is authored that covers them, and this review now does cover them, so 'reviewed' is defensible for them from this revision onward - but the note explaining what 'reviewed' means is not optional and is currently absent. (2) The durable repair is a control, not an edit: a rule that reports any record whose lifecycle_status is 'reviewed' with no covering review record, so the 22 - and any future instance - is visible on every run instead of only when a reader happens to compare a field against the coverage dimension. The 19 that carry no note are the priority subset. Referred to the verification and corpus-tooling owners. This review changed nothing: any edit to a test_measure record changes its content digest and invalidates every stored review digest over it, so the record repair is a revision with re-derived digests and belongs to the owner. The control is a tools/ change and is outside this review's write scope.

Accepted. Correct the attribution in oracle_detail.why_this_oracle: either cite the actual propagation site, ltc_6813-1.c:3114-3130, where PEC_valid gates both the store of cellVoltage_mV and the setting of invalidCellVoltage, or attribute line 641 to LTC_SaveVoltages, which is the function that contains it and whose branch handles the open-wire case rather than the PEC case. While the record is being revised, the residual_risk is the natural place to name the one configuration dependency the oracle rests on, namely that LTC_DISCARD_PEC is (false) in ltc_6813-1_cfg.h:106, since the same function marks a corrupted frame VALID when that macro is true. Referred to the verification owner. This review changed nothing: the fix is an edit to a test_measure record, which is a revision plus digest re-derivation and is not this review's write scope.

Accepted. For each of the five records, give the negative or absence case an entry in expected_outcomes, following the pattern the same family already uses in FB2-VER-TMS-000021, -000024 and -000028, where the distinguishing case is recorded as a count with an explicit unit (0 frames, 0 occurrences, 0 entries). Two named instances are the minimum: FB2-VER-TMS-000003 needs an outcome for the 4900 mV rejection, and FB2-VER-TMS-000001 needs one for the 4100 mV non-fault. FB2-VER-TMS-000002 needs more than an added outcome, because its step 1 defers to a state table the record does not contain; either carry the table or restate the step as an enumerated transition list. Separately, the per-record tolerances and timing objects in these five are template constants rather than values about the measure, and FB2-VER-TMS-000001's stated accuracy objective has no tolerance at all; a reader should not have to guess which numbers in these records are about the test. Referred to the verification owner. This review changed nothing.

Accepted. Two records, two edits, following the convention the same family already uses: express the bounded assertions so that tolerance carries the comparison, as FB2-VER-TMS-000028 does with expected_value 'at least 1' and tolerance 'at least'. Under that convention a latency ceiling is tolerance 'at most' with a numeric expected_value of 50 and 80 respectively, rather than a relational string carrying tolerance 'exact'. Referred to the verification owner. This review changed nothing.

results_summary.statement: Coverage went up by the identifiers this review names and by nothing else. The findings do not close on their own: no test_measure record was edited, so no step, expected outcome, threshold, oracle, digest or source anchor changed, and every stored review digest over these records still verifies. The family is split by quality, not uniformly: the eight records dated 2026-10-02 are the best-grounded test measures in this corpus on the evidence of this pass, seven distinct source citations of which six verify to the exact line, while the five dated 2026-09-13 are template instances whose oracles do not measure their own stated objectives. A single family-level verdict would have been wrong in both directions.
results_summary.findings_corrected_note: BOTH CORRECTIONS ARE RECORDED HERE BECAUSE THEY POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS AND THE POINT IS THAT THE DISCIPLINE IS THE SAME FOR EACH. (1) WITHDRAWN: this review first raised, against FB2-VER-TMS-000021, that a PEC mismatch might not gate invalidCellVoltage at all - in which case the record's expected outcome corrupted_frames_consumed_unchallenged = '0' would be unreachable and the record's central claim false. A second read of the same file located the propagation at ltc_6813-1.c:3114-3130, where PEC_valid gates both the store of the value and the setting of the flag, and confirmed LTC_DISCARD_PEC is (false) in the pinned configuration, so the branch the record relies on is the branch the build takes. The claim was therefore sound and the candidate finding was NOT A DEFECT. It is withdrawn rather than softened, and what survives of it is only the citation-attribution defect recorded as FB2-REV-FND-000175. Had it been reported at the severity the first reading implied, it would have asserted that a record was false when the corpus says nothing of the kind. (2) CORRECTED: the same review nearly reported a second, larger defect on the same evidence - that ltc_6813-1.c contains two definitions of DATA_CopyData, at line 123 and line 164, on the reading that the record cites a duplicate or shadowed function. A second read showed line 123 is the forward DECLARATION and line 164 is the definition, with no conditional compilation between them, and the record cites 164-196, which is the definition and its closing brace. That candidate is also withdrawn. Both corrections are recorded because a review that over-claims is the same defect as a review that under-claims, and because a reader comparing this record against the corpus should be able to see that the two discrepancies were found, checked, and found not to be defects rather than never noticed.

PARTIAL SCOPE, AND THE PART NOT COVERED IS THE LARGER PART. The uncovered population in this profile and the other is 128 records over 128 identifiers; this review covers 13. NOT REACHED: 12 requirement records (FB2-HW-TSR-000001 to -000003, FB2-SW-SIR-000001 to -000006, FB2-SW-SWR-000001 to -000003), 12 singleton-family records across 11 families, 35 finding records, 18 scenario records, 20 review records and 12 execution records. The 35 finding records are arguably the highest-value group remaining, because a finding is review output and reviewing one is a meta-review; they were not reached here because reading 35 records was not affordable in this pass, and a review that certifies without reading would be worse than no review. That is a statement about budget, not a judgement that the unreviewed groups are in better shape - FB2-REV-FND-000174 shows the unreviewed population is where the corpus's largest unmeasured honesty gap sits.

THE COVERAGE FIGURE UNDERSTATES THE UNCOVERED POPULATION, AND THIS REVIEW'S OWN CONTRIBUTION IS A WORKED EXAMPLE. The automated_review_coverage dimension builds its numerator and denominator from UNIQUE ID STRINGS: index_ids is a set of the id half of the (profile, id) key, so the 323 records of this corpus collapse to 284 identifiers, 39 of which are carried by two records each. A record can therefore be entirely unreviewed while the dimension reads as covered, because an as_is record shares its identifier. That is exactly the case for the five older records in this review: FB2-VER-TMS-000001 to -000005 were already inside the covered numerator, which is why the coverage figure did not move for them, and they were unreviewed all the same. Measured on this tree: 284 unique identifiers, 195 covered records, 182 covered identifiers, 128 uncovered records, 128 uncovered identifiers of which 26 are counted as covered because the sibling profile's record is reviewed. So the 102 that the dimension's denominator-minus-numerator reports is 26 short of the real figure of 128. This review does not treat that as one of its four findings, because its findings array is about records it read and no covered record is the locus of a measurement defect in the tool; it is recorded here instead, and it is the single most consequential thing this review learned.
No test_measure record was edited, revised or re-hashed by this review. The four findings are dispositions for the owner; every stored review digest over the reviewed records still verifies.

Source grounding was re-derived for the citations the records themselves state. It was NOT re-derived for every threshold the records assert: the SOA voltage limits, the debounce window of 100 ms, the 4200 mV limit in FB2-VER-TMS-000001, the 4900 mV and 3300 mV stimuli and the contactor figures in FB2-VER-TMS-000004 and -000025 were read as the record states them and were not each traced to a configuration constant at the pin. The two arithmetic claims that were checked are FB2-VER-TMS-000022's 50 ms period, re-read from the parameter registry where FB2-PRM-000003 carries value 50 with tolerance min 49 max 51, and the 1000/50 = 20 arithmetic, which is correct.

The eight newer records were read for what they claim and for how well they are grounded. This review did not re-derive the requirement-side acceptance criteria they verify, because those requirements are outside its scope and six of the twelve uncovered requirement records are among the population this review did not reach. A defect in a requirement would not be found by this pass even where a measure under review verifies it.

Nothing here constitutes a verification result. No module was executed, no timing, coverage or throughput measurement of any test_measure record exists as a result of this review, and no target hardware was used, powered or commanded. The eight newer records each state that the paired execution record is blocked, and this review did not contradict that.

This review asserts no ISO 26262 conformity, no certification, no tool qualification, no ASPICE capability level, no ASIL determination for the real product, no human approval, no production authorisation and no product verification credit.

THIS REVIEW REPRODUCES THE DEFECT IT REPORTS, AND THE HONEST FIGURE IS THEREFORE 18, NOT 17. FB2-REV-FND-000174 measures 22 records asserting lifecycle_status 'reviewed' with no covering review. This review covers the five of them named in the finding, so the population falls to 17 - and then this review's own record enters it, because a review record carries lifecycle_status 'reviewed' and a review record cannot cover itself. The population as it stands after this review is 18: 14 with no covering review and no lifecycle_status_note, and 4 with no covering review but a note. This record is one of those 4, and it is in the mitigated class only because it carries a lifecycle_status_note saying in terms what 'reviewed' means here. So the control FB2-REV-FND-000174 asks for has a second reason to exist: as written it would catch a review record asserting its own completion. The figures were re-measured after the fact by an independent checker written for this pass that imports nothing from corpus.py; it reproduced 19 silent and 3 noted before this review and 14 silent and 3 noted plus this record after it, from its own index walk.
